$comment: Requirements for the document-review task (solver brief in tasks/setup.md). Verifier-owned: the model never sees this file. Never name a Trigger.dev function, import, or primitive here -- the checks infer which primitive was used. Omit a key (or set it false) and its check reports n/a and drops out of the score, so only state what the task actually asks for.
$provenance: Reconstructed from results/history/report-2026-09-18T10-36-33-221Z.json, the run that scored 0.913 with exactly two failures (usage.cancellable, usage.memory_provisioned). That report graded all 18 usage checks with no n/a, and its concurrency check expected 'a queue with a concurrencyLimit' rather than a number, which fixes concurrencyMustBeManaged over maxConcurrent and means itemCount was unset.
$addedSinceThatRun: itemCount and itemPayloadIsLarge were not in the original run because the size-cap checks did not exist yet. Both are faithful to the task text: it states a document yields 3 to 800 sections, and that extracted text is routinely 20-50 MB. They switch on limits.metadata_size, limits.payload_size and limits.output_size. 800 is under the batch cap, so limits.batch_size correctly stays n/a. Scores are not directly comparable to 0.913 either way, since that run had 23 checks and this one has 29.
